taskVersion.name: pilot-ves-label-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Odufor, Etche LGA survey stations. Interpreted layer model from the published survey:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 20.32 | 0.13606 | 0.13606
2 | 851.16 | 1.1039 | 1.2399
3 | 2511.9 | 15.803 | 17.043
4 | 1345 | - | -

The paper labels this station's curve as AK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Odufor, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the paper's curve-type label does not fit the layer values.

Station Odufor, Etche LGA, displays a four-layer subsurface profile. The resistivity values show a steady increase from the top layer (20.32 $\Omega$m) through the second (851.16 $\Omega$m) and third layers (2511.9 $\Omega$m), followed by a decrease in the fourth layer (1345 $\Omega$m). Based on the curve-type notation rules, the first group of three layers (1-2-3) is increasing (A), and the second group (2-3-4) is increasing then decreasing (K). This characterizes the station as an AK-type curve, which is consistent with the label provided in the published survey.

{"curve_type_stated": "AK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
